paper_metadata.title: Parameter Setting in Quantum Approximate Optimization of Weighted Problems

summary: The paper derives analytical scaling rules for QAOA parameters for weighted optimization problems. On a dataset of 34,701 weighted MaxCut graphs (≤20 nodes), the proposed parameter rescaling achieves solutions on average only 1.1 percentage points worse than fully optimized parameters. For a portfolio optimization benchmark (7–20 qubits), rescaling the objective improves the convergence of the classical BOBYQA optimizer by reducing iterations by about 7.4×.

experiments.description: QAOA parameter-setting and performance evaluation for weighted MaxCut on random weighted regular and non-regular graphs, comparing proposed rescaling rules against prior parameter-transfer heuristics and direct optimization.

algorithm.variant: QAOA with transverse-field mixer for weighted MaxCut parameter setting
algorithm.optimizer: local optimizer (not specified); direct optimization used as baseline

parameter_setting_methods: proposed rescaling using arctan(1/sqrt(D-1)) for p=1-inspired rule
prior work parameter transfer from Ref. [9]

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Parameters set by analytical rescaling rules from unweighted MaxCut parameters; direct optimization used for comparison

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary spin variable in MaxCut Ising/QAOA formulation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize weighted cut value C(z)=1/2 sum_{(u,v) in E} w_uv (1 - z_u z_v)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints beyond MaxCut objective; handled via QAOA cost Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: C = 1/2 sum_{(u,v) in E} w_uv (i - z_u z_v)

problem_instance.description: Weighted MaxCut on a dataset of 34,701 weighted graphs, including regular and non-regular graphs, up to 20 nodes

dataset_specification.description: Graphs with up to 20 nodes; edge weights i.i.d. from Uniform[0,1], Uniform[-1,1], Exponential(lambda=0.2), and Cauchy

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Weights rescaled by dividing by sqrt((1/|E|) sum_{(u,v) in E} w_uv^2) for proposed method; alternative arctan-based rescaling also tested
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Median approximation ratios and optimality gaps evaluated across graphs, p values, and weight distributions; comparison to optimized parameters and prior parameter-transfer method

hardware.framework: QAOAKit / Qiskit (inferred from dataset and cited tooling)

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Approximation ratio and optimality gap computation

experiments.description: QAOA with xy mixer for constrained portfolio optimization, using objective rescaling to improve optimizer convergence on random portfolio instances.

hyperparameters.problem: mean-variance portfolio optimization with budget constraint
hyperparameters.mixer: xy mixer B = 1/2 sum_j (x_j x_{j+1} + y_j y_{j+1})
hyperparameters.initial_state: uniform superposition over all Hamming-weight k states (Dicke state)
hyperparameters.rescaling: divide objective by sqrt(sum of squared coefficients) including linear and quadratic terms

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Started from optimal QAOA parameters for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model: gamma_init = 1, beta_init = pi/4

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x q x^T Sigma x - mu^T x subject to sum_j x_j = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Equality constraint enforced by xy mixer and Dicke-state initial state

dataset_specification.description: 20 instances for each qubit count from 7 to 20; q=0.5; k=floor(n/2)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Objective reformulated in spin variables and rescaled using coefficient norm including linear terms mu_j and quadratic terms Sigma_ij
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: BOBYQA local optimization from fixed initial point; performance profiles over 280 instances; compare original vs rescaled objective and variant ignoring linear-term weights

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Rescale objective coefficients; convert portfolio problem to spin form; prepare Dicke initial state
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Recover optimum and compare iteration counts; compute performance profiles

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: rescaled landscape easier to optimize; original landscape flat

speedup_claims.baseline_method: BOBYQA on the original (unrescaled) portfolio objective
speedup_claims.conditions: xy-QAOA with p=1 on 280 random portfolio instances of size 7 to 20 qubits; fixed initial point gamma_init=1, beta_init=pi/4; xtol=ftol=1e-8
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in classical optimizer iterations, not a quantum runtime speedup. The optimizer recovered the same optimum in 91% of cases for both original and rescaled objectives.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: No asymptotic complexity claim; empirical improvement in optimizer convergence

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; experiments simulate xy-QAOA with p=1 on 7–20 qubits
limiting_factors: Improvement measured only in classical optimizer iterations (7.4× fewer)
No comparison with classical portfolio optimization solvers
No runtime or scaling advantage demonstrated
